user_query: Consumer rights overview
legal_text_raw: Under Section 2(9) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, consumer rights include: (i) right to be protected against marketing of hazardous goods and services; (ii) right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price; (iii) right to be assured access to variety of goods at competitive prices; (iv) right to be heard and represented; (v) right to seek redressal against unfair trade practice or exploitation; and (vi) right to consumer awareness.
layman_explanation:
Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Indian law guarantees 6 core consumer rights:
• Right to Safety & Information: Protection against hazardous goods and complete transparency regarding price, purity, and expiry dates.
• Right to Choose & Be Heard: Freedom to select competitive products and represent your grievances before forums.
• Right to Redressal & Education: Legal entitlement to refund, replacement, or compensation for defective items or deficient services via the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or e-Daakhil portal.

user_query: An e-commerce website refuses to refund my money for a damaged phone delivered in an open box, citing their no-return policy.
legal_text_raw: Rule 5 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 mandates that every e-commerce entity shall effect all refunds within a reasonable period of time. Under Section 2(47), no entity shall engage in unfair trade practices including arbitrary cancellation penalties or refusal to accept returns of defective goods.
layman_explanation:
A 'no-return policy' cannot override statutory law. Under the E-Commerce Rules 2020:
• You are legally entitled to a 100% refund or replacement for damaged, defective, or misdescribed products.
• The seller/platform cannot impose arbitrary cancellation or refusal charges.
• You can immediately lodge a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (Call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915) or file on e-Daakhil.

user_query: What are the pecuniary limits and where can I file a consumer court case in India?
legal_text_raw: District Commission has jurisdiction for claims up to ₹50 Lakhs (revised 2021). State Commission has jurisdiction for claims between ₹50 Lakhs and ₹2 Crores. National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has jurisdiction for claims exceeding ₹2 Crores.
layman_explanation:
The Consumer Protection Act establishes a three-tier dispute redressal system based on claim value:
• District Commission: Handles claims up to ₹50 Lakhs.
• State Commission: Handles claims from ₹50 Lakhs up to ₹2 Crores.
• National Commission (NCDRC): Handles claims exceeding ₹2 Crores.
• You can file complaints online from anywhere in India using the e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) without hiring a lawyer.

user_query: A pressure cooker exploded in my kitchen causing severe burn injuries due to a manufacturing flaw. Can I sue the manufacturer for damages?
legal_text_raw: Chapter VI introduces Product Liability. A product manufacturer, service provider, or seller shall be liable to compensate the consumer for any harm or injury caused by a defective product, manufacturing defect, or failure to give adequate usage warnings.
layman_explanation:
Yes, under the 'Product Liability' provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:
• The manufacturer and seller are strictly liable to pay compensation for physical injuries, medical expenses, and property damage caused by a defective product.
• You do not need to prove negligence—proof of defect and resulting harm is sufficient.
• Preserve the damaged appliance, hospital medical bills, and purchase receipt to claim compensation before the District Consumer Commission.

user_query: An airline cancelled my flight at the last minute without offering alternative booking or hotel stay. Can I claim compensation for deficiency of service?
legal_text_raw: Deficiency under Section 2(11) means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in quality, nature, and manner of performance required by law or contract. DGCA Passenger Charter mandates full refund, meal refreshments, and compensation up to ₹10,000 for unnotified cancellations.
layman_explanation:
Yes, last-minute flight cancellations without support constitute 'Deficiency of Service':
• Under DGCA Passenger Charter and CPA 2019, the airline must offer an alternate flight or full immediate refund plus compensation up to ₹10,000 depending on flight duration.
• You can claim reimbursement for hotel stay, food, and wasted connecting bookings.
• File an immediate grievance on AirSewa portal (airsewa.gov.in) and National Consumer Helpline (1915).

user_query: What are dark patterns in online shopping apps, and are they illegal under Indian consumer law?
legal_text_raw: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 issued under CPA 2019 prohibit deceptive design practices including false urgency, basket sneaking, confirm shaming, forced action, and subscription traps as unfair trade practices.
layman_explanation:
Dark patterns are manipulative design tricks used by apps to cheat consumers, and they are strictly illegal in India:
• Common illegal tricks: False urgency ('Only 2 left in stock!'), basket sneaking (automatically adding insurance or donation fees to cart), and hidden cancellation buttons.
• CCPA guidelines categorize these as Unfair Trade Practices under Section 2(47).
• You can report deceptive apps directly to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or CCPA.

user_query: A builder delayed flat possession by 4 years despite taking 95% payment. Can I approach the Consumer Court instead of RERA?
legal_text_raw: The Supreme Court in Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni (2020) held that remedies under the Consumer Protection Act and RERA are concurrent and alternate. Homebuyers have the statutory right to seek refund with interest or delayed possession compensation before Consumer Commissions.
layman_explanation:
Yes, homebuyers can approach either Consumer Court or RERA:
• The Supreme Court affirmed that CPA 2019 and RERA are concurrent remedies—you are free to choose the Consumer Commission.
• You can claim full refund of money paid along with 9%–12% annual interest or monthly delayed compensation.
• If the property value plus compensation is under ₹50 Lakhs, file in District Commission; between ₹50 Lakhs and ₹2 Crores in State Commission.
